name: Cromo Vasquez-Inoue
description: Cromo Vasquez-Inoue began as a back-alley chrome installer in Tier 2's Fabricator District before turning their own body into a living portfolio — currently running 34 distinct augmentation systems, more than half of which were self-installed. Their SynFeed channel 'OPEN CHASSIS' documents every installation in real time, including the two that went catastrophically wrong on camera. Unlike corporate aug-fluencers, Cromo sources exclusively from unlicensed fabricators, black-market military surplus, and salvaged industrial systems, and names every supplier openly.
cultural_impact: Cromo has single-handedly normalized 'visible chrome' aesthetics in Tier 2-3 spaces, where augmentation was previously kept subtle or hidden to avoid profiling. Their open-sourced installation guides have been downloaded an estimated 4 million times and are cited in at least three documented cases of successful emergency self-surgery on the Shelf.
key_figures: Dr. Amara Osei-Brandt (licensed surgeon who publicly criticized and then quietly consulted)
locations: The Chassis Bar — an aug-community venue, Tier 2
story_hooks: One of Cromo's openly named black-market suppliers has gone missing, and the last package they sent contained components that don't match any known augmentation schematic — Cromo has installed it and something is different, though they can't say what.

A Tier 4 corponation aug-brand wants Cromo to front a campaign — not for money, but in exchange for a rare military-grade spinal system that could fix nerve damage Cromo has been living with for three years. Cromo is visibly tempted.
A follower who used Cromo's open-source guide to self-install a neural interface has developed a rare cascade rejection — and their family is holding Cromo publicly responsible.
controversy: During a 2221 live installation stream, Cromo's spinal relay failed mid-procedure — they lost motor control of their lower body for eleven minutes on camera. They finished the installation themselves, regained function, and the clip has been watched over 200 million times. Licensed medical corponations demanded the stream be pulled; SynFeed declined.
